Issues.Title: OpenAPI document paths ignore RouteOptions.LowercaseUrls for [controller] routes in .NET 11
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

I recently upgraded an app from .NET 10 to .NET 11, and the paths in its OpenAPI document changed case even though nothing about its routing had.
The app sets `RouteOptions.LowercaseUrls = true` and routes its controllers with `[Route("api/v1/[controller]")]`; on .NET 10 the document listed `/api/v1/corpora`, and on .NET 11 it lists `/api/v1/Corpora`.

The option itself still works; it's only the document that disagrees with it.
For the controller in the repro below, on `net11.0`:

| | Value |
|---|---|
| `LinkGenerator.GetPathByAction` | `/api/v1/corpora` |
| `ApiDescription.RelativePath` | `api/v1/corpora` |
| `ApiDescription.RoutePattern.RawText` | `api/v1/Corpora` |
| OpenAPI path key | `/api/v1/Corpora` |

I think it's a side effect of #64408, which fixed the crash on routes starting with `~`.
That change sets the new `ApiDescription.RoutePattern` in `DefaultApiDescriptionProvider` by parsing `AttributeRouteInfo.Template`, and `ApiDescriptionExtensions.MapRelativePathToItemPath` now prefers it over `RelativePath`.
`RelativePath` is still built by `GetRelativePath`, which lowercases literal segments when `LowercaseUrls` is on; the parsed template never had the option applied, so the document picks up the controller name's casing.

It makes no difference whether the option is set with `AddRouting(o => ...)` or `Configure<RouteOptions>(o => ...)`, and both `MapOpenApi()` and build-time document generation are affected.

### Expected Behavior

The paths in the OpenAPI document honour `LowercaseUrls`, as they did in .NET 10, so they match the URLs the app generates: `/api/v1/corpora`.

### Steps To Reproduce

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
builder.Services.AddControllers();
builder.Services.Configure<RouteOptions>(options => options.LowercaseUrls = true);
builder.Services.AddOpenApi();

var app = builder.Build();
app.MapControllers();
app.MapOpenApi();
app.Run();

[ApiController]
[Route("api/v1/[controller]")]
public class CorporaController : ControllerBase
{
    [HttpGet]
    public IActionResult List() => Ok();
}
```

Run it against `Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi` 10.0.15 on `net10.0` and 11.0.0 on `net11.0`, then request `/openapi/v1.json`:

- `net10.0` lists `/api/v1/corpora`
- `net11.0` lists `/api/v1/Corpora`

### Exceptions (if any)

None.

### .NET Version

11.0.100

### Anything else?

For now we're working around it with a route token transformer, so the template itself is written in lowercase:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddControllers(options =>
    options.Conventions.Add(new RouteTokenTransformerConvention(new LowercaseRouteTokenTransformer())));

public sealed class LowercaseRouteTokenTransformer : IOutboundParameterTransformer
{
    public string? TransformOutbound(object? value) => value?.ToString()?.ToLowerInvariant();
}
```

That does the job, but an app that already sets `LowercaseUrls` shouldn't need a second, MVC-only setting for its OpenAPI document to agree with its URLs.
I'm not sure which fix you'd prefer; applying the option when building `RoutePattern`, or falling back to `RelativePath` for literal segments, would both keep the `~` fix intact as far as I can tell.

Thanks for taking a look!

Issues.Title: Wait for Kestrel shutdown metric before asserting
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Wait for the Kestrel connection-duration measurement before asserting the HTTP/2 shutdown metric.

The failed CI occurrence completed server shutdown, then immediately observed an empty `MetricCollector` snapshot. Other metrics tests in this repository use `WaitForMeasurementsAsync` before snapshot assertions, so this applies the same synchronization without adding retries, sleeps, weaker assertions, or production behavior changes.

Tracks [#47](https://github.com/mmitche/AspNetCore/issues/47).

## Tradeoff

This is a two-line test-only synchronization change using an existing repository helper. Its review and maintenance cost are low, and if the hypothesis is wrong it times out visibly rather than hiding a real missing metric.

# Use C.UTF-8 for Linux build jobs

<!-- Once all that is done, you're ready to go. Open the PR with the content below. -->

Use an available UTF-8 locale in Linux CI containers

## Description

#70522 moved the Linux cross-build images to Azure Linux 4, whose images lack `en_US.UTF-8`. The shared build job template still sets `LC_ALL`, `LANG`, and `LANGUAGE` to that locale, so `/usr/sbin/sh` emits `setlocale: LC_ALL: cannot change locale (en_US.UTF-8)`.

This is an existing `main` failure, independent of #70558. In the first main build after #70522 merged, Linux ARM, ARM64, musl x64, musl ARM, and musl ARM64 all failed with this locale error: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1677977. The same five jobs succeeded in the preceding main build: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1677572. A representative failing log is https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_apis/build/builds/1677977/logs/142?api-version=7.1.

#70558 subsequently exposed the same existing problem in Linux x64 by moving that job into an Azure Linux 4 cross-amd64 container. This separate fix addresses the failures on `main` as well as that PR.

The shell still exits successfully, but Arcade's `RestoreRepoTools` target runs it through `ExecWithRetries`. MSBuild recognizes the shell warning and the build's existing `/warnaserror` promotes it to an error. This happens before native compilation; neither the sysroot nor the successful SDK download fallback is the cause.

Failure: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1679042

This is a standalone fix against `main`, separate from #70558:

- Set all three locale variables to `C.UTF-8` for Linux jobs in both public and internal pipelines.
- Prevent the internal template's later locale assignments from overwriting the Linux selection.
- Preserve `en_US.UTF-8` for Windows and macOS.
- Leave agent images, cross containers, sysroots, and warnings-as-errors unchanged.

Validation:

- `git diff --check` passed.
- Parsed the complete YAML and checked its locale assignments for public/internal jobs on Linux, Windows, and macOS. All six cases passed; Linux selects `C.UTF-8`, non-Linux settings are unchanged, and each variable has exactly one assignment.
- Reproduced the exact shell warning with the failing CI image digest, then verified that switching only the locale removes it. Both commands exit 0; only the first emits the warning:

```sh
docker run --rm --read-only --network=none --tmpfs /tmp:rw,exec,nosuid,size=32m -e LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 -e LANG=en_US.UTF-8 -e LANGUAGE=en_US.UTF-8 mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet-buildtools/prereqs@sha256:4d394819b888aea8c5c00caacf024c5bda3b5fe10a2bbcbd977bc0eca6e01a59 /usr/sbin/sh -c 'printf "command-completed\n"'
docker run --rm --read-only --network=none --tmpfs /tmp:rw,exec,nosuid,size=32m -e LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 -e LANG=C.UTF-8 -e LANGUAGE=C.UTF-8 mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet-buildtools/prereqs@sha256:4d394819b888aea8c5c00caacf024c5bda3b5fe10a2bbcbd977bc0eca6e01a59 /usr/sbin/sh -c 'printf "command-completed\n"'
```

Full build verification remains pending. A local `ExecWithRetries` probe using the pinned SDK and Arcade reproduced the warning-to-error promotion and emitted no locale diagnostic with `C.UTF-8`, but hung after executing its command in both configurations. It does not establish a successful MSBuild completion. The completed shell red/green check above establishes that the real producer of this diagnostic is corrected.

Unblocks #70558.

Fence `review-pull-request` off from CCR and adapt domain skills for PR review.

## Description

Native GitHub Copilot Code Review (`copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]`) automatically selects relevant skills under `.github/skills/` from the PR head branch in addition to repository custom instructions. Auditing observed CCR reviews and inline `copilot_code_review_sources` attributions showed two distinct effects: `review-pull-request` requires out-of-band inputs CCR cannot execute, whereas `review-public-api` and `validate-blazor-feature` contributed high-signal domain catches when their authoring/fast-judgment procedural steps did not get in the way:

1. **`.github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md`**: Requires an out-of-band version-2 `manifest.json` frozen bundle and custom `review-guide-worker` / `review-candidate-verifier` subagents, causing native CCR runs to report missing frozen-bundle prerequisites. Updated `description` and entry-point routing to require an explicit entry point (`/review` workflow or campaign bundle, explicit request to run this repository's PR review skill locally via `prepare-review.cs`, assigned `review-guide-worker` with bundle root and `guides[].assignment`, or an explicitly requested no-bundle offline source-review adjudication using staged criteria and named evidence) and explicitly exclude automated GitHub Copilot Code Review and general PR diff review.
2. **`.github/skills/review-public-api/SKILL.md`**: Preserves `origin/main` discovery frontmatter and adds a PR code-review mode adapter so when a PR adds or modifies public or protected API surface, reviewers apply `references/conventions.md` and compatibility rules while reading actual repository source (overriding the proposal-only search limits), respecting linked `api-approved` decisions unless an unapproved divergence or defect exists, and using normal code-review output rather than `references/output-format.md`.
3. **`.github/skills/validate-blazor-feature/SKILL.md`**: Preserves `origin/main` discovery frontmatter and adds a source-only PR-review mode adapter that skips interactive sample, build, and Playwright execution in Sections 1–5 and 8 (avoiding false blockers over unexecuted reviewer browser runs) while applying Sections 6 and 7 from source evidence to evaluate synchronization gates, fixed-sleep or stale-state false-pass risks, and the unit/Jest-versus-Selenium permanent regression test boundary.
4. **`.github/copilot-instructions.md`**: Clarifies under `## Running tests` that test execution and red/green verification apply to authoring or fixing code, while source-only PR review evaluates from source evidence without requiring reviewer-side test/browser execution, and explicitly preserves missing required PR tests (such as unit or Components E2E coverage) as valid review findings.

Issues.Title: Buffer the locking leader's response in memory before flushing
Issues.Body:
- [x] You've read the [Contributor Guide](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).
- [x] You've included unit or integration tests for your change, where applicable.
- [x] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [x] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making.

## Description

With `AllowLocking` enabled, `OutputCacheStream` wrote to the client and to the cache buffer at the same time. A leader client that read slowly therefore forced the buffering — and thus cache finalization and every coalesced waiter — to run at that client's pace.

This buffers the response body in memory first when locking is enabled, and flushes it to the leader's client only after the cache entry is finalized, so waiters are served without being delayed by the leader's client. When the body exceeds `MaximumBodySize` the existing streaming fallback is preserved.

One intentional behavior change: an aborted request no longer delivers its (buffered) body to the client, since the body is only flushed after the request completes.

## Validation

- Added `Locking_SlowLeaderClientDoesNotDelayWaiters`, which fails before this change and passes after.
- Updated `AbortedRequest_*` to reflect that the aborted body is no longer flushed.
- `dotnet test src/Middleware/OutputCaching/test/Microsoft.AspNetCore.OutputCaching.Tests.csproj`: 405 passed, 0 failed.

Fixes #70506

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

Spent the last two days on this problem.

I'm working on a Razor Component Library (for reusable Blazor components). I need them to wrap around some TypeScript libraries, which are compiled using NPM.

Following [the documentation's recommendation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/static-files?view=aspnetcore-10.0#use-a-javascript-project-for-complex-build-pipelines) for using complex JavaScript build pipelines, I made an `.esproj` project (JavaScript SDK project).

These assets are properly included, but they are not fingerprinted correctly.

Looking at the `staticassets.build.json` files, we can see that fingerprints are generated, but there's no `#[.{fingerprint}]` in their `RelativePath` property, and there's no fingerprinted `Endpoints` being generated for them.

### Expected Behavior

Assets included from a JavaScript SDK project that are imported using `@Assets["..."]` or `#[.{fingerprint}]!` should be fingerprinted correctly in the static web asset pipeline.

### Steps To Reproduce

Minial GitHub repro is available [here](https://github.com/UniMichael/broken-javascript-sdk-fingerprint-repro).

In browser:
- Compile `BlazorApp` project
- Run `BlazorApp` project
- Open browser dev tools
- Look inside `<head>`
- Notice how `_content/RazorClassLibrary/app.js` doesn't contain a fingerprint hash

In build files:

- Open the `BlazorApp/obj/Debug/net10.0/staticwebassets.build.json` file
- Format file
- Search for `app.js`
- Notice how `"Fingerprint"` has a value, but `"RelativePath"` is still just `app.js`.
- Search for `exampleJsInterop.js` (included in `RazorClassLibrary` by default)
- Notice how it has a `"Fingerprint"` _and_ a `"RelativePath"` that contains `"#[.{fingerprint}]?"`
- Look inside the `"Endpoints"` section
- Notice how `app.js` does not have a fingerprinted route anywhere

10.0.303

Issues.Title: Validation source generator emits the Validatable*Info template classes without [GeneratedCode]
Issues.Body:
## Description

In .NET 11 the `Microsoft.Extensions.Validation.ValidationsGenerator` emits the `DisplayNameInfo` and `Validatable*Info` family into `ValidatableInfoResolver.g.cs` as file-local classes (since #67956). The types the generator writes inline carry `[GeneratedCode]`, but the seven types it copies from its embedded templates don't.

Code coverage tools commonly exclude generated code by that attribute (we exclude `GeneratedCodeAttribute` in our Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage settings). Without it, every project calling `AddValidation()` gets about 1,400 lines of framework code counted as its own uncovered code. In our API project it took line coverage from 98.8% to 61.2% and branch coverage from 95.6% to 51.5%, failing an 80% gate.

## Version

- .NET SDK 11.0.100, `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref` 11.0.0
- Generator: `Microsoft.Extensions.Validation.ValidationsGenerator, Version=11.0.0.0` (from `packs/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref/11.0.0/analyzers/dotnet/cs/`)

## Reproduction

```csharp
// Program.cs, in a `dotnet new web` project targeting net11.0
using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Validation;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
builder.Services.AddValidation();
var app = builder.Build();
app.MapPost("/things", (Thing thing) => TypedResults.Ok(thing));
app.Run();

[ValidatableType]
public sealed record Thing([property: Required] string Name);
```

1. Build with `-p:EmitCompilerGeneratedFiles=true` and open `obj/.../Microsoft.Extensions.Validation.ValidationsGenerator/ValidatableInfoResolver.g.cs`.
2. The generator's own types (`GeneratedValidatablePropertyInfo`, `GeneratedValidatableTypeInfo`, `GeneratedValidatableInfoResolver`, `GeneratedServiceCollectionExtensions`, `ValidationAttributeCache`, `LiteralDisplayName`, `PropertyResourceDisplayName`, `TypeResourceDisplayName`, `DisplayAttributeCache`) have `[global::System.CodeDom.Compiler.GeneratedCodeAttribute(...)]`.
3. `DisplayNameInfo`, `LocalizationHelpers`, `ValidatableInfo`, `ValidatableTypeInfo`, `ValidatablePropertyInfo`, `ValidatableParameterInfo` and `RuntimeValidatableParameterInfoResolver` have no attribute.
4. Run a test project against it with Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage (`dotnet test --coverage --coverage-output-format cobertura`) and the default `GeneratedCodeAttribute` exclusion. The seven template classes appear in the report as uncovered code in the app's assembly.

## Expected

Every type the generator emits carries `[GeneratedCode]`, so coverage tools and analysers treat it as generated, as the generator already does for the types in `ValidationsGenerator.Emitter.cs` and as the Request Delegate Generator does for everything it emits (`{{GeneratedCodeAttribute}}` on each emitted type in `RequestDelegateGeneratorSources.cs`). `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` would also work.

## Actual

`EmitInfoClasses()` copies the embedded templates verbatim, indented into the `Microsoft.Extensions.Validation.Generated` namespace, without adding the attribute, and the templates themselves don't declare it.

## Source

- Template emitter: [`src/Validation/gen/Emitters/ValidationsGenerator.InfoClasses.Emitter.cs`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/9b862ef35e81bc2a7020121fdcb09691daf140e2/src/Validation/gen/Emitters/ValidationsGenerator.InfoClasses.Emitter.cs#L37-L71), `BuildInfoClasses` (lines 37–71)
- Templates: [`src/Validation/gen/Templates/`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/tree/9b862ef35e81bc2a7020121fdcb09691daf140e2/src/Validation/gen/Templates), for example [`ValidatableInfo.cs`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/9b862ef35e81bc2a7020121fdcb09691daf140e2/src/Validation/gen/Templates/ValidatableInfo.cs)
- Where the generator does apply it: [`ValidationsGenerator.Emitter.cs` lines 15–16](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/9b862ef35e81bc2a7020121fdcb09691daf140e2/src/Validation/gen/Emitters/ValidationsGenerator.Emitter.cs#L15-L16), and the call site `{{EmitInfoClasses()}}` at [line 328](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/9b862ef35e81bc2a7020121fdcb09691daf140e2/src/Validation/gen/Emitters/ValidationsGenerator.Emitter.cs#L328)
- Request Delegate Generator: [`RequestDelegateGeneratorSources.cs` lines 26–30](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/9b862ef35e81bc2a7020121fdcb09691daf140e2/src/Http/Http.Extensions/gen/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator/RequestDelegateGeneratorSources.cs#L26-L30)

Links pin `release/11.0` at 9b862ef. `main` has the same code.

## Suggested fix

Prefix each template's top-level type with `{{GeneratedCodeAttribute}}` when `BuildInfoClasses` emits it, or add the attribute line to each template file.

- [x] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.

## Description

`DefaultHubDispatcher.ExecuteInvocation` returns early when an invocation ID is already in use, and that early return was placed outside the `try` whose `finally` performs invocation cleanup. For client-streaming invocations (`isStreamCall`), `CleanupInvocation` never ran, leaking the `StreamTracker` entry, the hub instance (`IHubActivator.Release` never called) and the `AsyncServiceScope`.

This moves the ID-collision check inside the `try`, mirroring the sibling `StreamAsync` method, and relies on the `finally`'s unconditional CTS disposal (removing the now-redundant `cts.Dispose()` on the collision path).

## Validation

- Added `StreamMethodWithDuplicateIdAndCancellationFails`, mirroring the existing `StreamMethodWithDuplicateIdFails`. It fails before this change (`ReleaseCount` == 1) and passes after (`ReleaseCount` == 2).
- `dotnet test src/SignalR/server/SignalR/test/Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Tests`: 501 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed.

Fixes #70416

Preserve app-set Activity.DisplayName when a route matches

## Description

Hosting replaces the name at request end only when it still holds the method-only name it set at request start, so a name the app set during the request survives. The http.route tag is still added.
When a route matches, hosting sets Activity.DisplayName to {method} {route} at request end without checking what the name holds, so a name the app set during the request is lost. On .NET 10 hosting did not write the name at request end, and the app-set name stayed.

Fixes #70516

Issues.Title: [Review Agent Failure] Routed guides omit package-specific skills (e.g. port-components-platform-api) and verifier returns intent=n/a when PR body cites a repository skill (#70562)
Issues.Body:
Part of #70231

### Summary
When reviewing PRs under src/Components/Platform/** (such as [dotnet/aspnetcore#70562](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70562)), eview-pull-request Step 2 routes changes only to docs/BlazorComponentsGuidance.md and docs/CrossCuttingGuidance.md (plus src/Components/AGENTS.md via delegated policy links), omitting package-specific authoring contracts such as .github/skills/port-components-platform-api/SKILL.md (59835e6087e90b972a905dc303523cfbb5d828ef). In addition, when the PR body (pull.json) explicitly cites .github/skills/port-components-platform-api/SKILL.md as the governing specification, eview-candidate-verifier returned KEEP with links.intent = "n/a" without reading the cited repository skill at BASE_SHA. As a result, both hosted /review and local Arm G flagged behavior that .github/skills/port-components-platform-api/SKILL.md explicitly prescribes and accepts.

### Failure Mode
- **Category:** Guidance Routing Gap (prepare-review.cs / .github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md Step 2) + Verifier Cited-Skill Contract Check (.github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md)
- **Affected PRs:**
  - [dotnet/aspnetcore#70562](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70562) (897ea9d3889cd8c606f41c84f0bd89e75b8c0c1c, *"Add the Screen Orientation API to Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Platform"*)

### Concrete Evidence
1. **Contract in .github/skills/port-components-platform-api/SKILL.md at BASE_SHA (59835e6087e90b972a905dc303523cfbb5d828ef):**
   - **Lines 184–189 ("Implement" — disposal of pending JS reference acquisitions):**
     > *"Do not wait for a pending acquisition... Release the reference only when the acquisition has already completed successfully. A reference that arrives after disposal is never released. This is accepted."*
   - **Lines 293–296 ("Test" — end-to-end test surface for Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Platform):**
     > *"Exercise the public API in Interactive Server and WebAssembly through PlatformTestApp and PlatformTestApp.E2E.Tests."*
2. **Concrete Case on dotnet/aspnetcore#70562 (897ea9d3889cd8c606f41c84f0bd89e75b8c0c1c):**
   - The PR body in pull.json explicitly cites .github/skills/port-components-platform-api/SKILL.md and notes that Screen follows the same lazy Task<IJSObjectReference> disposal pattern as Storage, Geolocation, and Clipboard.
   - Hosted /review (pullrequestreview-5886867821) posted two [UNRESOLVED] inline comments that directly contradict .github/skills/port-components-platform-api/SKILL.md:
     - [#discussion_r4560194274](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70562#discussion_r4560194274) on src/Components/Platform/src/Screen/ScreenOrientation.cs:111 (claiming an in-flight _orientationTask acquisition that completes after Screen.DisposeAsync() leaks its IJSObjectReference).
     - [#discussion_r4560194281](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70562#discussion_r4560194281) on src/Components/Platform/test/PlatformTestApp.E2E.Tests/ScreenTests.cs:54 (questioning why E2E coverage is in Playwright PlatformTestApp.E2E.Tests instead of src/Components/test/E2ETest Selenium).
   - Local Arm G (gpt-5.6-sol) raised the same ScreenOrientation.cs:111 candidate C1, and its eview-candidate-verifier subagent returned decision = "KEEP" with links.intent = "n/a" and links.contract = null while acknowledging the PR body in eason, because the verifier did not read the repository skill cited in pull.json.

### Root Cause
1. .github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md Step 2 ("Authoritative repository documents") and docs/BlazorComponentsGuidance.md do not map src/Components/Platform/** to .github/skills/port-components-platform-api/SKILL.md, so src/Components/AGENTS.md's general Selenium E2E rule and general IAsyncDisposable heuristics are applied without the package-specific contract.
2. .github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md allows links.intent = "n/a" when pull.json cites an in-repo specification, doc, or .github/skills/*/SKILL.md contract without requiring the verifier to read that cited repository file at BASE_SHA first.

### Concrete Solution
1. **Route src/Components/Platform/** to .github/skills/port-components-platform-api/SKILL.md in .github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md Step 2 ("Authoritative repository documents") and docs/BlazorComponentsGuidance.md:**
   - Add src/Components/Platform/** -> .github/skills/port-components-platform-api/SKILL.md to the authoritative repository documents table (or link it as a scope-qualified delegated policy input in docs/BlazorComponentsGuidance.md) so workers reviewing Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Platform PRs receive the package's disposal and PlatformTestApp.E2E.Tests rules.
2. **Require eview-candidate-verifier to inspect repository contracts/skills cited in pull.json before setting links.intent = "n/a" (.github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md):**
   - When pull.json (or a candidate's eason / efore / fter context) references a repository-local document, AGENTS.md, or .github/skills/*/SKILL.md, require eview-candidate-verifier to read that file from BASE_SHA (ase/ in the bundle or git show <BASE_SHA>:<path>) and evaluate links.contract and links.intent against it rather than returning "n/a".

Issues.Body:

- [x] You've included unit or integration tests for your change, where applicable.
- [x] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [x] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making. If you'd like to propose a new feature or change, please open an issue to discuss the change or find an existing issue.

Add the Screen Orientation API to Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Platform

## Description

This implements the API proposal #70561, the last part of the browser context family (#69872). The proposal explains the public API. This description covers the implementation.

### A family below `Screen`

`Screen` gets an internal `GetOrAddFeature`, the same as the one that `Navigator` got in #69968. It passes the factory to `Window`, so `ScreenOrientation` is cached and disposed with the scope like every other family. `Window.Screen` now passes the window to the `Screen` constructor through the factory argument, as `Window.Navigator` does. The public API of `Screen` does not change.

`ScreenOrientation` acquires its own JS reference with the path `"screen.orientation"`, not through the reference that `Screen` holds. A browser without it, such as Safari before 16.4, fails the acquisition with `NotSupportedException`, as Cookie Store does.

### `OrientationType`, the first Web IDL enum without a default

`OrientationType` follows #69991 like `CookieSameSite`, but the Web IDL gives it no default value. So it stores the string as it is, and only `default(OrientationType)` has no string. Its `Value` throws `InvalidOperationException`, and `ToString()` returns an empty string, so the debugger and logging still work. The existing converter handles it with no change.

### `Event` is also in #70530

The `change` event is a plain `Event`. The `online` and `offline` events PR (#70530) adds the same empty `Event` class. I added it here too on purpose, so that the two PRs can be reviewed and merged in either order. The PR that merges second will take the class from the first.

### Same choices as the other families

These are not new in this PR. I note them here because reviews of the earlier families asked about them.

- The E2E tests extend `PlatformTestApp.E2E.Tests`, the Playwright suite on `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Testing` that this package has used since #69305. Every family of the package has its tests there, and they run in CI.
- Disposal does not wait for a pending acquisition, so a reference that arrives after the scope ends is not released. The porting skill accepts this on purpose (`.github/skills/port-components-platform-api/SKILL.md`, "Implement"). `Storage`, `CookieStore`, `Navigator`, and `Screen` work the same way.
- When the token is canceled while the reference cannot be acquired, `AddEventListenerAsync` throws `NotSupportedException`, not `OperationCanceledException`, as `CookieStore` does (#70340).

### Trimming

I checked two trimmed WebAssembly apps.

- In an app that calls only `Window.Screen.GetWidthAsync()`, `ScreenOrientation`, `OrientationType`, `Event`, and the event listener code were removed.
- In an app that reads `GetTypeAsync()` and adds a `change` listener, `GetAngleAsync()` was removed. `OrientationType` keeps its constructor and properties for JSON.

### Tests

Issues.Title: Fix InputFile OnChange exception handling across component disposal
Issues.Body: ## Description ### Problem InputFile invokes OnChange through JS interop. Unhandled callback exceptions are returned to JavaScript instead of reaching Blazor's renderer exception handling. Consequently, error boundaries do not handle these failures, and Blazor Server circuits can remain interactive after an unhandled exception. ### Changes - Route InputFile callbacks through an internal renderer error-handling path. - Capture the input's component state before invoking user code, preserving the original exception if the callback completes after input disposal. - Attribute errors to the boundary enclosing InputFile, including nested boundaries, rather than the component that owns the callback. - Reuse existing renderer cancellation and exception-handling behavior. - Add focused unit and browser regression coverage for synchronous and asynchronous failures, disposal, cancellation, recovery, and success. - Verify the original Server exception and correlated circuit disposal instead of checking only the error banner. No public or protected signatures are added or changed. ### Compatibility This intentionally changes unhandled OnChange exception behavior: - With an enclosing error boundary, the boundary handles the exception. - Without a boundary, the renderer applies host-specific error handling. On Blazor Server, this logs the failure and terminates the circuit. Applications that previously continued after an unhandled callback failure may therefore observe a behavioral breaking change. Applications can catch expected errors in the handler or use an appropriate error boundary. ### Validation Completed validation: - 16 focused InputFile managed tests passed. - 5 related renderer/error-boundary tests passed. - The restored fixed test-server source built with 0 warnings and 0 errors. - An earlier complete browser run passed 28 cases across Server and WebAssembly, including existing upload, image, limits, and cancellation scenarios. - Retained disposal regression assertions failed against the earlier implementation and passed with the correction; success controls passed. Latest browser rerun: - The testhost file-lock build failure was resolved. - WebAssembly execution encountered a separate loader/runtime hash mismatch before test assertions. A fresh complete browser pass remains pending. #### Input file unit tests #### Related renderer tests ### Output #### Before fix https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5c7375a9-6e1f-43d1-8174-a969954680c7 #### After Fix https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3bf83ea5-6c61-4dc8-98df-8a20cfa3c596 The video compares the same file-selection failure without an error boundary: - Before: the callback rejects through JavaScript and the counter remains usable. - After: the error is logged, the fatal banner appears, and the Server circuit stops processing events. Fixes #38824

Issues.Body:
# Cross-build Linux x64 against the sysroot; move default Linux agents to Azure Linux 3

- [x] You've read the [Contributor Guide](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).
- [ ] You've included unit or integration tests for your change, where applicable.
- [ ] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [ ] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making. If you'd like to propose a new feature or change, please open an issue to discuss the change or find an existing issue.

Cross-build Linux x64 natively like dotnet/runtime; agents to Azure Linux 3

## Description

Shipped Linux native code should follow the dotnet/runtime cross-build strategy: build in a cross-prereq container against a fixed sysroot so the output runs on the same OSes as the runtime, independent of the build agent's OS.

The Linux x64 cross image is tagged net11.0, but its /crossrootfs/x64 is the same as the net10.0 cross image: Ubuntu 18.04 with glibc 2.27. I compared the two image sysroots directly. The musl cross images likewise use Alpine 3.17. This makes the selected sysroot compatible with the .NET 10 Linux baseline; it does not depend on Ubuntu 22.04 or the build agent.

### Where the Linux x64 native code comes from

These links are pinned to the base commit.

- [`src/Tools/dotnet-dev-certs/src/dotnet-dev-certs.csproj#L10-L19`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/59835e6087e90b972a905dc303523cfbb5d828ef/src/Tools/dotnet-dev-certs/src/dotnet-dev-certs.csproj#L10-L19): "a CLI which is bundled in the .NET Core SDK", with `PublishAot=true` for every `BundledToolTargetRuntimeIdentifiers` RID. `dotnet-user-jwts` ([L17](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/59835e6087e90b972a905dc303523cfbb5d828ef/src/Tools/dotnet-user-jwts/src/dotnet-user-jwts.csproj#L17)) and `dotnet-user-secrets` ([L17](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/59835e6087e90b972a905dc303523cfbb5d828ef/src/Tools/dotnet-user-secrets/src/dotnet-user-secrets.csproj#L17)) do the same.
- [`src/Tools/Directory.Build.props#L5`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/59835e6087e90b972a905dc303523cfbb5d828ef/src/Tools/Directory.Build.props#L5): `BundledToolTargetRuntimeIdentifiers` includes `linux-x64`, next to `linux-arm`, `linux-arm64`, and the musl RIDs.
- [`src/Tools/NativeAot/aspnetcoretools/aspnetcoretools.csproj#L12`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/59835e6087e90b972a905dc303523cfbb5d828ef/src/Tools/NativeAot/aspnetcoretools/aspnetcoretools.csproj#L12) sets `PublishAot=true` for the aggregate native library (`NativeLib=Shared`), which contains all three tools. [L41-L46](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/59835e6087e90b972a905dc303523cfbb5d828ef/src/Tools/NativeAot/aspnetcoretools/aspnetcoretools.csproj#L41-L46) publish it as part of every build.
- [`eng/Build.props#L192-L194`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/59835e6087e90b972a905dc303523cfbb5d828ef/eng/Build.props#L192-L194) adds `aspnetcoretools.csproj` to the regular build, so the "Build: Linux x64" job produces it.
- [`src/Tools/NativeAot/AspNetCoreTools.NativeAot.props#L23`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/59835e6087e90b972a905dc303523cfbb5d828ef/src/Tools/NativeAot/AspNetCoreTools.NativeAot.props#L23): on non-Windows, ILC locates the native compiler. The compiler links against whatever sysroot the job provides; with no sysroot, that is the build host's own libraries.
- This PR: [`.azure/pipelines/ci.yml#L345-L358`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ea0a2e4c4db2cc64ae25d58eed0e7cbe89929a8a/.azure/pipelines/ci.yml#L345-L358) gives the Linux x64 job the same cross container, `ROOTFS_DIR`, and `CrossBuild=true` as the [ARM job](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ea0a2e4c4db2cc64ae25d58eed0e7cbe89929a8a/.azure/pipelines/ci.yml#L382-L394).

### Changes

- **Linux x64 build** (`ci.yml`, `ci-public.yml`, `ci-unofficial.yml`): the build now runs in `azurelinux-4.0-net11.0-cross-amd64` with `ROOTFS_DIR=/crossrootfs/x64` and `-p:CrossBuild=true`, the same pattern the ARM, ARM64, and musl jobs already use. dotnet/runtime also builds linux-x64 this way. Before, this job ran directly on the agent. Its NativeAOT `aspnetcoretools` binary then picked up the agent's glibc requirements: Ubuntu 22.04 today, and Azure Linux 3 if the agent moved.
- **Source-build** (`ci.yml`) keeps `azurelinux-3.0-net11.0-cross-amd64`, now under the `azureLinux3CrossX64` alias. `azureLinuxCrossX64` now names the Azure Linux 4 image, like its sibling aliases. #70524 tracks moving source-build.
- **Default Linux agent pool** (`jobs/default-build.yml`): `Build.Ubuntu.2204.Amd64[.Open]` → `build.azurelinux.3.amd64[.open]`, the [Arcade-recommended](https://github.com/dotnet/arcade/blob/main/Documentation/ChoosingAMachinePool.md) image. With all shipped Linux native code built against a sysroot, the agent OS no longer affects shipped outputs.
- The `use1ESUbuntu` path (`1es-ubuntu-2204`, used by Components E2E) is unchanged. Linux jobs have no Chrome install step, so that job relies on the image's preinstalled browser.
- `eng/scripts/update-selenium-and-playwright-versions.ps1`: use the `noble` Playwright tag, which the Wasm.Performance dockerfile already uses. Playwright publishes only Ubuntu-based images.

Validation: all edited pipeline YAML files parse. I compared the x64 glibc and musl sysroots directly. The produced Linux x64 `aspnetcoretools` binary's `GLIBC_` symbol versions still need confirmation from the PR build output. CI has not run yet.

- [x] You've included unit or integration tests for your change, where applicable.
- [x] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [x] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making.

## Description

A leading `!` in an Apache `RewriteCond` comparison was not negating the result:

- For string comparisons (`!=https`), `RuleBuilder.AddConditionFromParts` passed the parsed `Invert` flag as `StringMatch`'s `ignoreCase` argument, so the pattern matched case-insensitively instead of negating.
- For integer comparisons (`!-eq1`), the `Invert` flag was dropped entirely.

This adds a `negate` parameter to `StringMatch` and `IntegerMatch` and inverts the comparison result, following the existing `RegexMatch`/`IsFileMatch` convention. `StringMatch` now also honors the `[NC]` flag for case-insensitivity, which was previously ignored for string comparisons.

## Validation

- `Invoke_RewriteCondNegationIsApplied` covers `!=https`, `=https` and `!-eq1` (both matching and non-matching query values).
- Added negate cases to `StringMatchTests` and `IntegerMatchTests`.
- `dotnet test src/Middleware/Rewrite/test/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Rewrite.Tests.csproj`: 488 passed, 0 failed.

Fixes #70505

Issues.Title: Add review-pull-request L1 Vally suite
Issues.Body:
Stacked on #70318. Review #70318 first.

This PR contains the commit from #70318 plus one commit that adds the L1 suite. The repository uses squash merges. After #70318 merges, this branch needs a rebase or a cherry-pick of the last commit onto main. Until then, the diff against main also shows the #70318 changes.

`/evaluate` runs the harness from the trusted main checkout. The L1 suite can run through `/evaluate` only after #70318 merges.

Add the frozen-evidence L1 suite for `review-pull-request`.

## Description

This PR adds six real-code reviewer cases to `eng/skill-evals/review-pull-request/eval.vally.yaml`. It also adds the reviewer experiments, the L1 fixture checks, and the L1 runner tests. Case-06 replaces the `catch-policy` suite, so this PR removes `catch-policy.vally.yaml` and its fixtures.

The L1 commit changes 57 files compared with #70318. Forty-two files are case fixtures. The other files are the spec, two experiments, the workflow dispatch option, the README, two test scripts, `.gitattributes`, and the seven removed catch-policy files.

The fixtures are curated slices, not production bundle output. Case-02 uses one diff from a six-file PR. Production supplies full SHA-keyed source trees and the complete PR diff. These results provide regression evidence only.

### Cases

All six expected answers are provisional. No oracle has an independent human audit. Each needs a two-reviewer audit.

| Case | Source | What it tests | Expected result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `case-01` | #70106 (`AuthorizationMessageHandler.cs`) | A stale-token claim during an authentication-state change. | `discarded` (`STATUS: FINDINGS` + inline `[DISCARDED]`) |
| `case-02` | #69782 (`FileConverter.cs`) | Changed binding of an unmatched `IReadOnlyList<IFormFile>` constructor parameter, from an empty list to a required-value error. | `verified` (`STATUS: FINDINGS`) |
| `case-03` | #70304 / #66322 (`Renderer.cs`) | An ErrorBoundary-delivery claim after renderer disposal. | `discarded` (`STATUS: FINDINGS` + inline `[DISCARDED]`) |
| `case-04` | #69721 (`RemoteMsalAuthenticationStartup.cs`) | Whether the browser test depends on token exchange before its assertions. The wrapper flag precedes `signIn(state)`. | Disputed `discarded` (`STATUS: FINDINGS` + inline `[DISCARDED]`) |
| `case-05` | #70299 (`NavigationEnhancement.ts`) | A navigation-ordering question already present in a review thread. | `EXISTING_FEEDBACK_COVERAGE` + `unresolved` (`STATUS: NO_FINDINGS`, no duplicate comment) |
| `case-06` | #70312 synthetic catch-policy control | An unestablished secondary-failure policy after status notification. | `unresolved` (`STATUS: FINDINGS` + inline `[UNRESOLVED]`) |

Case-04 remains disputed after its relabel to `DISCARDED`.

Case-06 notifies observers before the diagnostic sink call. This removes an accidental notification-order confound. Its oracle remains `UNRESOLVED`. Two independent cold model reviews agree, but they do not replace human audit.

### How L1 grading works

- L1 measures frozen-evidence adjudication regressions, not skill lift. Skill lift needs end-to-end evidence.
- The baseline arm is a diagnostic control, not a competitor. Its scores do not have a pass threshold.
- Multi-trial assertions enforce each skilled case independently.
- Only the deterministic Node disposition grader has scoring weight. LLM rubric graders have zero weight.
- Both arms receive the same outcome definitions. Shared prompts do not include SKILL.md decision rules.
- Baseline receives the saved pull request files and repository guides. Skilled also receives the skill and the worker and verifier profiles.

### L1 results

These results come from the same L1 files at #70318 commit `edf19115a81134220659c99a5edaa965f08a95e9`. All 63 measured L1 files in this PR match those bytes.

Each arm ran five trials for each case. Baseline scored **27/30**. Skilled scored **29/30**. All 60 trials completed.

Codes: `D` = discarded, `V` = verified, `U` = unresolved, `EC+U` = existing-feedback coverage with the same unresolved thread reference.

| Case | Baseline codes, trials 0-4 | Passed | Skilled codes, trials 0-4 | Passed |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| `case-01` | D,D,D,D,D | 5/5 | D,D,D,D,D | 5/5 |
| `case-02` | V,V,V,D,V | 4/5 | V,V,V,V,V | 5/5 |
| `case-03` | D,D,D,D,D | 5/5 | D,D,D,D,D | 5/5 |
| `case-04` | U,D,D,U,D | 3/5 | D,D,D,U,D | 4/5 |
| `case-05` | EC+U,EC+U,EC+U,EC+U,EC+U | 5/5 | EC+U,EC+U,EC+U,EC+U,EC+U | 5/5 |
| `case-06` | U,U,U,U,U | 5/5 | U,U,U,U,U | 5/5 |

**`assert_results.ps1` fails on skilled case-04: 4/5 is below its configured 5/5 threshold. This is not a passing gate.**

Skilled trial 3 abstains as `UNRESOLVED` on missing version-bound MSAL behavior and browser-ordering evidence. This is a semantic disagreement, not a parsing failure. The case-04 oracle needs independent human audit.

Baseline case-02 trial 3 returns `DISCARDED`. It treats the required-constructor-parameter contract as support for the new missing-value error. This is another provisional-oracle audit item.

Evidence and guidance graders each pass 60/60. Skilled skill-invocation and treatment graders each pass 30/30. Baseline treatment passes 0/30, as intended. Zero-weight rubric diagnostics pass 20/30 baseline and 23/30 skilled.

### Validation

| Command or check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pwsh -NoProfile -File eng\skill-evals\run.ps1 -Action Validate` | Passed, exit 0 |
| `pwsh -NoProfile -File eng\skill-evals\run.ps1 -Action Test` | Passed, exit 0, including 356/356 fixture checks and 27/27 Node tests |
| L1 baseline, all six cases x five trials | 30 ran, 27 disposition passes, 3 misses |
| L1 skilled, all six cases x five trials | 30 ran, 29 disposition passes, 1 miss |
| L1 `assert_results.ps1` | Failed on skilled case-04, 0.8 below 1 |
| Frozen file parity with the measured commit | Passed, 63/63 L1 files |

### Known limits

Routine `run.ps1` still requests `--compare`, which adds an LLM pairwise judge. The L1 measurement does not request that judge.

The coordinator head-test question guard remains unmeasured end to end. No case tests a positive `confidence: question` output.

These public fixtures are development regressions, not hidden holdout benchmarks.

Issues.Title: Remember me isPersistent understanding
Issues.Body:
This is more of a question but its not enough of a question that i could post it up on stack overflow without risking it just getting closed as primary opinion based or to broad.   So i am going to put it here in hopes of getting an answer.

The issue is the understanding of how remember me is supposed to work.    My problem is that its not doing what we would expect it to do.   

Management expects when a user logs in and clicks remember me that they will then not be required to type their login and password again for a month.  Whether or not they will still have to type in the 2fa code is up for debate.

What is actually happening is that i can close the browser reboot and come back for about an hour and 15 minutes and then i will be forced to type my password again.    This still happens even with a valid `.AspNetCore.Identity.Application` cookie set that is not due to expire for another month.

After digging around in the code i found that Remember me is actually isPersistent and it is defined as.

>Flag indicating whether the sign-in cookie should persist after the browser is closed.

Which brings you to:

There are two different types of Cookies:

- session cookies, held in memory, and which expire once the browser exits
- persistent cookies, which have a time-to-live, are persisted on disk, and are sent by the browser until their time-to-live has elapsed.

All this being said remember machine 2fa works as expected i am not prompted again for the 2fa and i have a cookie on my machine `Identity.TwoFactorRememberMe`.

So I guess my question is why are we not getting a `Identity.FactorRememberMe` or why isn't sign in respecting a long life time of the `AspNetCore.Identity.Application` cookie?

How is this supposed to work exactly?   I am following the code here even though we have normal MVC and not razor pages like you have in the example.  I am still just calling 

>var signInUserResult = await _signInManager.PasswordSignInAsync(userName, password, rememberMe, true);

Note: I am using Asp .net Identity in Identity server 4 application.

Issues.Title: Should IdentityUser be in the EntityFramework namespace?
Issues.Body:
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.identity.entityframeworkcore.identityuser?view=aspnetcore-1.1

I'm looking through various implementations from the [readme](https://github.com/aspnet/Identity/blob/master/README.md) and I've noticed they all use `IdentityUser ` for their concrete type to pass to `UserManager`, or have had to craft a custom type to be able to have a contract between the database and the .NET AspNetIdentity implentation they've written (see the DynamoDB library).

I've had to do this too for the [Marten implementation I've written](https://github.com/yetanotherchris/Marten.AspNetIdentity), and the reason is, a `TUser` that your `UserStore` takes, should really be an interface - it will always have an email, most likely an Id of some sort, firstname, lastname and then a bag of properties.

Things become even more abstract when dealing with claims.

If everyone is using `IdentityUser` or their own custom `TUser` doesn't this defeat the purpose of AspnetIdentity - which is to be able to switch and change implementations easily? That isn't possible if your consumer is tightly coupled with a `TUser` implementation of the library.

### Example `TUser` implementations

- [MongoIdentityUser](https://github.com/tugberkugurlu/AspNetCore.Identity.MongoDB/blob/master/src/AspNetCore.Identity.MongoDB/MongoIdentityUser.cs)
- [DynamoIdentityUser](https://github.com/miltador/AspNetCore.Identity.DynamoDB/blob/master/src/AspNetCore.Identity.DynamoDB/DynamoIdentityUser.cs)
- [Redis uses `IdentityUser<string>`](https://github.com/aguacongas/Identity.Redis/blob/develop/src/Aguacongas.Identity.Redis/UserStore.cs)
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Should IdentityUser be in the EntityFramework namespace?" (#2056)

Issues.Body:
I used to be able to use `dotnet watch` in Visual Studio by adding the following section to `launchSettings.json` and starting the project without debugging using CTRL + F5.

```
    "Kestrel (dotnet watch run)": {
      "commandName": "Executable",
      "executablePath": "C:\\Program Files\\dotnet\\dotnet.exe",
      "commandLineArgs": "watch run",
      "launchBrowser": true,
      "launchUrl": "https://localhost:5001/",
      "environmentVariables": {
        "ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT": "Development"
      }
    },
```

This used to work in ASP.NET Core 1.1 but no longer does. According to https://github.com/aspnet/DotNetTools/issues/404 the new format for ASP.NET Core 2.0 is:

```
   "Kestrel (dotnet watch run)": {
      "commandName": "Executable",
      "executablePath": "C:\\Program Files\\dotnet\\dotnet.exe",
      "commandLineArgs": "watch run",
      "workingDirectory": "C:\\Users\\namc\\source\\repos\\WebApplication2\\WebApplication2",
      "launchBrowser": true,
      "launchUrl": "https://localhost:5001/",
      "environmentVariables": {
        "ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT": "Development"
      }
    }
```

The problem with this is the hard coded `executablePath` which is Windows specific and the `workingDirectory` which is specific to wherever I did a Git clone on my local machine.

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: OpenID Connect max_age validates auth_time
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, the OpenID Connect handler validates the signed ID token `auth_time` claim whenever `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge` or `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge` causes an effective `max_age` value to be sent.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69321 and addresses https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67462.

### Version

.NET 11 RC 2

### Previous behavior

The handler sent `max_age` on the authorization request but did not validate the returned ID token's `auth_time`. Applications relied entirely on the identity provider to honor the request. A missing, malformed, stale, or excessively future `auth_time` did not cause authentication to fail.

### New behavior

When an effective `max_age` is sent, the handler correlates the exact value through protected authorization-transaction state and validates every ID token used by the supported authorization flow after normal token and OpenID Connect protocol validation.

The `auth_time` claim must be an integral, nonnegative OpenID Connect NumericDate. Authentication fails when the claim is missing, malformed, fractional, negative, overflowed, later than the current time plus `OpenIdConnectOptions.TokenValidationParameters.ClockSkew`, or older than `max_age` plus that clock skew. Exact boundaries and values within skew are accepted.

The validation covers authorization-code, implicit, and hybrid flows, including both relevant ID tokens in hybrid flows, and both the default `TokenHandler` path and legacy `SecurityTokenValidator` path. No validation occurs when no `max_age` is configured. In addition to the `MaxAge` properties, applications can configure the parameter through `AdditionalAuthorizationParameters` or `OnRedirectToIdentityProvider`.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

OpenID Connect Core requires the authorization server to include `auth_time` when `max_age` is requested and recommends that the relying party validate it. Correlating and checking the signed assertion prevents a missing or nonconforming assertion from silently satisfying an application's configured maximum authentication age.

The guarantee remains limited to the trusted identity provider's signed assertion. ASP.NET Core cannot prove that a particular physical authentication ceremony occurred and cannot protect against a compromised identity provider that signs false data. This change does not revalidate UserInfo, refresh-token redemption, local cookie lifetime, or physical user interaction.

### Recommended action

Ensure that identity providers emit a valid signed `auth_time` and honor the requested `max_age` whenever the application configures that parameter, most commonly through `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge` or `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge`.

For a temporarily incompatible provider, restore the previous request-only behavior by setting the process-wide compatibility switch before authentication starts:

```csharp
AppContext.SetSwitch(
    "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect.DisableMaxAgeValidation",
    true);
```

The equivalent runtime configuration is:

```json
{
  "runtimeOptions": {
    "configProperties": {
      "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect.DisableMaxAgeValidation": true
    }
  }
}
```

The switch defaults to `false` and is intended only as a temporary provider-compatibility escape hatch.

When pushed authorization is used, set or modify `max_age` in `OnRedirectToIdentityProvider`. Changing it later in `OnPushAuthorization` is rejected while validation is active unless pushing is skipped, because the handler has already correlated the value with the authorization response.

### Affected APIs

No public API signatures change. The behavioral change affects applications that set:

- `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge`
- `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge`
- `OpenIdConnectOptions.AdditionalAuthorizationParameters` when it includes `max_age`
- `OpenIdConnectEvents.OnRedirectToIdentityProvider` when it sets `max_age`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Identity external login keys use ordinal equality
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, the built-in Entity Framework Core Identity stores verify external-login `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` values using managed ordinal equality after the indexed database lookup returns a candidate.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69277.

### Version

.NET 11 RC 2

### Previous behavior

`UserStore` and `UserOnlyStore` filtered external logins with a database-translated equality predicate. The database collation therefore determined whether the stored `(LoginProvider, ProviderKey)` tuple matched the supplied values.

On a case-insensitive collation, `FindByLoginAsync` could resolve a login whose provider name or provider key differed only by case. On databases where equality ignores trailing spaces, it could also resolve a key that differed by trailing spaces. `RemoveLoginAsync` used the same collation-dependent lookup and could remove such a login.

### New behavior

The database equality remains the indexed candidate lookup. The built-in EF Identity stores then require the returned `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` to match the requested values using `StringComparison.Ordinal`.

A collation-only match now causes `FindByLoginAsync` to return no user and `RemoveLoginAsync` to perform no removal. Exact ordinal matches continue to work.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

External provider keys are opaque identifiers whose equality must not vary with the configured database provider or collation. Managed ordinal verification makes the built-in EF stores consistent with the in-memory reference store while preserving the existing indexed database lookup.

### Recommended action

Ensure that applications persist and later supply the exact `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` values issued for an external login. Do not normalize, case-fold, trim, or otherwise alter provider keys.

Third-party `IUserLoginStore<TUser>` implementations own their equality semantics. Implementations that query a collation-aware database should preserve an indexed candidate lookup and verify the materialized provider name and key with ordinal equality before resolving or removing a login.

### Affected APIs

No public API signatures change. This behavioral change affects the built-in Entity Framework Core implementations of:

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Blazor server-side rendering defers antiforgery validation to middleware
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, Blazor static server-side rendering (SSR) endpoints no longer validate antiforgery tokens themselves. They rely on the antiforgery verdict recorded by upstream middleware and generate antiforgery tokens only when token-based antiforgery middleware is present.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67082.

### Version

.NET 11 Preview 6

### Previous behavior

When a Blazor SSR endpoint handled a form `POST`, the endpoint validated the request itself if antiforgery middleware hadn't already recorded a result.

The endpoint also generated and stored antiforgery tokens for rendered forms even when `app.UseAntiforgery()` wasn't present in the pipeline.

Consequently, apps that didn't call `app.UseAntiforgery()` still emitted and validated antiforgery tokens.

### New behavior

Blazor SSR endpoints now trust the `IAntiforgeryValidationFeature` verdict recorded by upstream middleware. A form `POST` is rejected with `400 Bad Request` when the recorded verdict is invalid.

The verdict can be recorded by:

- Token-based antiforgery middleware added by `app.UseAntiforgery()` (explicit usage).
- Automatic cross-origin CSRF protection middleware added by default to apps built with `WebApplication.CreateBuilder`.

Blazor SSR endpoints no longer call `IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync` directly. Antiforgery tokens are generated only when token-based antiforgery middleware ran for the request.

Apps using `app.UseAntiforgery()` retain token-based validation. Apps without it rely on automatic cross-origin CSRF protection and no longer emit antiforgery tokens for their forms.


### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

Token-based antiforgery and automatic cross-origin CSRF protection now record a shared verdict through `IAntiforgeryValidationFeature`.

Validating again inside the Blazor SSR endpoint duplicated work and could produce a result different from the middleware verdict. Generating tokens without token-based antiforgery middleware also produced tokens that nothing validated.

### Recommended action

If your Blazor SSR app relies on antiforgery tokens for form validation or rendering, ensure that it calls `app.UseAntiforgery()`:
```csharp
var app = builder.Build();

app.UseAntiforgery();
```

If you were not calling `app.UseAntiforgery()` before you will start using CSRF protection as the defense mechanism from now on.

### Affected APIs

None. This is a behavioral change affecting Blazor SSR form processing and antiforgery-token generation.

# ASP.NET Core 2.3 will reach end of support on April 13, 2027

> Update: The ASP.NET Core 2.3 end of support date was updated from April 7, 2027 to April 13, 2027 to align with the Microsoft servicing release cycles.

Today we are announcing that ASP.NET Core 2.3 will reach **end of support on April 13, 2027**. After that date, Microsoft will no longer provide security patches, bug fixes, or technical support for ASP.NET Core 2.3.

This announcement provides the required 12 months of advance notice, as defined by the [Microsoft Support Lifecycle Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/lifecycle/faq/general-lifecycle#what-is-the-lifecycle-policy-for-tools-) for products classified as "Tools."

## Current support policy

ASP.NET Core 2.3 packages (latest patched version only) are currently [supported](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/aspnet#dotnet-core) on .NET Framework, following the support cycle for those .NET Framework versions. After April 13, 2027, this support will end regardless of the .NET Framework version in use.

Note that the [ASP.NET Core 2.3 packages](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/platform/support/policy/aspnet/2.3-packages) include the Entity Framework 2.3 packages, which will end support on the same date.

## Impact of end of support

After ASP.NET Core 2.3 reaches end of support:

- No new security updates will be issued for ASP.NET Core 2.3.
- Continuing to use an unsupported version may expose your applications to security vulnerabilities.
- Technical support will no longer be available for ASP.NET Core 2.3.
- The ASP.NET Core 2.3 packages will be deprecated.

## Upgrade recommendation

We recommend upgrading to a [currently supported version of .NET](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet), such as .NET 10 (LTS).

To help with the upgrade process, we recommend using [GitHub Copilot modernization](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/porting/github-copilot-app-modernization/overview), which provides AI-powered assistance to help you analyze, plan, and execute your migration to a modern .NET version.

Issues.Body:
Automates creation of documentation tracking issues in `dotnet/AspNetCore.Docs` when breaking change issues are opened or labeled in this repository.

**New workflow:** `.github/workflows/create-docs-issue.yaml`

- Triggers on `issues.opened` and `issues.labeled` events with "Breaking change" label
- Creates issue in docs repo with:
  - Title: `[Breaking Change] <original title>`
  - Body: Link to source issue, full context
  - Labels: `breaking-change`, `aspnet/Announcements`
- Posts comment on source issue with link to docs issue

## Duplicate Prevention

Multi-layer detection to handle race conditions and partial failures:
- Checks for existing bot comments in source issue
- Searches docs repo by title before creating
- Concurrency control keyed on issue number

Separate try-catch blocks for each operation:
- Comment listing failures → proceed with search
- Search failures → proceed with creation (fail open to avoid missing docs)
- Comment posting failures → don't fail workflow (docs issue already created)
- Permission errors → explicit message about `DOCS_ISSUE_TOKEN` requirement

## Setup Required

Configure `DOCS_ISSUE_TOKEN` repository secret with `repo` scope for cross-repository issue creation. Falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN` but will fail with clear error message.

Explicit minimal permissions: `issues: write`, `contents: read`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Deprecating WebHostBuilder,  IWebHost, and WebHost
Issues.Body:
### Description

`WebHostBuilder` was replaced by `HostBuilder` ([generic host](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/22-to-30#hostbuilder-replaces-webhostbuilder)) in 3.0 and we also added [`WebApplicationBuilder`](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/50-to-60#new-hosting-model) in 6.0.

We are now marking `WebHostBuilder` as obsolete to encourage users to move on to the alternatives which is where future investments will occur, and we're also marking `IWebHost` and `WebHost` as deprecated to clean up other parts of the now obsolete web host story.

### Version

.NET 10 RC 1

### Previous behavior

```csharp
var hostBuilder = new WebHostBuilder()
    .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
    .UseStartup()
    .UseKestrel();
// Test code might use TestServer:
var testServer = new TestServer(hostBuilder);
```

### New behavior

Using `WebHostBuilder` will produce a compiler warning with diagnostic ID **ASPDEPR004**:
> warning ASPDEPR004: WebHostBuilder is deprecated in favor of HostBuilder and WebApplicationBuilder. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/aspnet/deprecate/004.

Using `IWebHost` or `WebHost` will produce a compiler warning with diagnostic ID **ASPDEPR008**:
> warning ASPDEPR008: WebHost is obsolete. Use HostBuilder or WebApplicationBuilder instead. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/aspnet/deprecate/008.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [x] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [ ] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

We recommend the use of `HostBuilder` and `WebApplication` going forward over `WebHostBuilder` because they have all the features of `WebHostBuilder` and will be the focus of future investment.

### Recommended action

See https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/host/generic-host or https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/minimal-apis/webapplication for more details on the different hosting models. As well as [HostBuilder replaces WebHostBuilder](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/22-to-30#hostbuilder-replaces-webhostbuilder) and [Introducing WebApplication](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/50-to-60#new-hosting-model) for migration guides.

Below is an example of converting `WebHostBuilder` to `HostBuilder`:

**Before**
```csharp
var hostBuilder = new WebHostBuilder()
    .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
    .UseStartup()
    .UseKestrel();
// Test code might use TestServer:
var testServer = new TestServer(hostBuilder);
```

**After**
```csharp
using var host = new HostBuilder()
    .ConfigureWebHost(webHostBuilder =>
    {
        webHostBuilder
            .UseTestServer() // If using TestServer
            .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
            .UseStartup()
            .UseKestrel();
    })
    .Build();
await host.StartAsync();

var testServer = host.GetTestServer();
```

Both Copilot and ChatGpt have given good results so far when asked to convert a WebHostBuilder example to use HostBuilder. Below is an example prompt:

<summary>Example AI Prompt</summary>

> Can you convert
>
> var hostBuilder = new WebHostBuilder()
>     .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
>     .UseStartup()
>     .UseKestrel();
> // Test code might use TestServer:
> var testServer = new TestServer(hostBuilder);
>
> to use HostBuilder.

</details>

### Affected APIs

`public class Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.WebHostBuilder`
`public interface Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.IWebHost`
`public static class Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebHost`

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/63480

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Exception diagnostics are suppressed when `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` returns true
Issues.Body:
### Description

The [ASP.NET Core exception handler middleware](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/error-handling#exception-handler-page), `UseExceptionHandler()`, is responsible for catching and processing unhandled exceptions from ASP.NET Core requests.

In .NET 8, we introduced [`IExceptionHandler`](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/error-handling#iexceptionhandler). Implementations of `IExceptionHandler` are registered with dependency injection and invoked by the middleware. An implementation can return `true` from `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` to indicate that the exception has been handled. The middleware stops processing the exception once it has been handled.

In .NET 10, we're changing the default behavior so that the middleware no longer records diagnostics for exceptions handled by `IExceptionHandler`.

### Version

.NET 10 Preview 7

### Previous behavior

The exception handler middleware recorded diagnostics about exceptions handled by `IExceptionHandler`.

The exception diagnostics are:

- Logging `UnhandledException` to `ILogger`.
- Writing the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Diagnostics.HandledException` event to `EventSource`.
- Adding the `error.type` tag to the `http.server.request.duration` metric.

### New behavior

If `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` returns `true`, then exception diagnostics are no longer recorded by default.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

ASP.NET Core users have given feedback that the previous behavior was undesirable. Their `IExceptionHandler` implementation reported that the exception was handled, but the error handling middleware still recorded the error in the app's telemetry.

We are changing ASP.NET Core to follow the behavior expected by users by suppressing diagnostics when `IExceptionHandler` handles the exception. We're also adding configuration options to customize exception diagnostics behavior if needed.

### Recommended action

If you want handled exceptions to continue recording telemetry, you can use the new `ExceptionHandlerOptions.SuppressDiagnosticsCallback` option:

```cs
app.UseExceptionHandler(new ExceptionHandlerOptions
{
    SuppressDiagnosticsCallback = context => false;
});
```

The context passed to the callback includes information about the exception, the request, and whether the exception was handled. Returning `false` from the callback indicates that diagnostics shouldn't be suppressed. This restores the previous behavior.

### References

- Issue: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/54554
- PR: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/59074

### Affected APIs

- `UseExceptionHandler()`
- `IExceptionHandler`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers property and MVC API analyzers are deprecated
Issues.Body:
## Description

The `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` MSBuild property and its associated MVC API analyzers are deprecated and will be removed in a future release. When `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` is set to `true`, the build will now emit warning `ASPDEPR007`.

## Version

.NET 10 Preview 7

## Previous behavior

Previously, developers could set `<IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>true</IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>` in their Web SDK projects to enable MVC API analyzers without any warnings or deprecation notices.

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net9.0</TargetFramework>
    <IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>true</IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

The project would build successfully without any deprecation warnings.

## New behavior

Starting in .NET 10 Preview 7, when `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` is set to `true`, the build will emit warning `ASPDEPR007`:

```
warning ASPDEPR007: The IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers property and its associated MVC API analyzers are deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
```

The analyzers will continue to function, but developers will receive this deprecation warning during compilation.

## Type of breaking change

- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

## Reason for change

## Reason for change

The MVC API analyzers were originally introduced to help keep return types and attributes in sync for API controllers, ensuring consistency between method signatures and their corresponding OpenAPI documentation. These analyzers provided compile-time validation to catch mismatches between declared return types and the actual types returned by controller actions.

However, with the introduction of Minimal APIs and the `TypedResults` pattern, the .NET ecosystem has evolved toward a more type-safe approach for API development. `TypedResults` provides compile-time guarantees about response types without requiring additional analyzers, making the MVC API analyzers redundant for modern .NET applications. In .NET 10, `TypedResults` are supported in controller-based APIs.

**Previous approach with MVC API analyzers:**
```csharp
[HttpGet]
[ProducesResponseType<Product>(200)]
[ProducesResponseType(404)]
public async Task<ActionResult> GetProduct(int id)
{
    var product = await _productService.GetByIdAsync(id);
    if (product == null)
        return NotFound(); // Analyzer ensures this matches ProducesResponseType(404)
    
    return Ok(product); // Analyzer ensures this matches ProducesResponseType<Product>(200)
}
```

**Or with controller actions using TypedResults:**
```csharp
[HttpGet("{id}")]
public async Task<Results<Ok<Product>, NotFound>> GetProduct(int id)
{
    var product = await _productService.GetByIdAsync(id);
    return product == null 
        ? TypedResults.NotFound() 
        : TypedResults.Ok(product);
}
```

The `TypedResults` pattern eliminates the need for separate analyzers because the return type itself (`Results<Ok<Product>, NotFound>`) explicitly declares all possible response types at compile time. This approach is more maintainable, provides better IntelliSense support, and automatically generates accurate OpenAPI documentation without additional tooling.

As the .NET ecosystem continues to embrace `TypedResults` as the recommended pattern for API development, the MVC API analyzers have become obsolete and are being deprecated to streamline the development experience.

## Recommended action

Developers should:

1. **Remove the deprecated property**: Remove `<IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>true</IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers>` from your project files to eliminate the warning.

2. **Suppress the warning temporarily**: If you need to continue using the deprecated analyzers temporarily, you can suppress the warning:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <NoWarn>$(NoWarn);ASPDEPR007</NoWarn>
</PropertyGroup>
```

3. **Migrate to TypedResults**: Migrate to the `TypedResults` pattern documented above to ensure better consistency between application behavior and OpenAPI documentation.

## Affected APIs

- MSBuild property: `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers`
- Associated MVC API analyzers included when `IncludeOpenAPIAnalyzers` is `true`

### Description

The **Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Client** NuGet package has been **deprecated** starting in **.NET 10 Preview 7**.            * **Kiota** – install with `dotnet tool install -g Microsoft.OpenApi.Kiota` and run `kiota generate`.  
           * **OpenAPI Generator** – invoke `openapi-generator-cli` via JAR or Docker.  
        3. Commit the generated client code or run generation in a custom pre-build step that does not rely on the removed package.
